title: ACA s. 11 — Appointment of arbitrators (ACA s. 11)

content.overview: Section 11 provides for appointment of arbitrators by the parties under an agreed procedure, and for court appointment when the agreed procedure fails or is not followed. The section is read with section 12 and the Schedules on independence and impartiality.
content.glance: Party-agreed appointment first; court appointment under s. 11 when the procedure fails; unilateral appointment by an interested party is impermissible.
content.study: Section 11 structures appointment by agreement and residual court power. After the 2015 amendments, independence and impartiality constraints (s. 12 and Schedules) inform who may act and who may appoint. Landmark cases restrict unilateral appointment by an interested party.

sections.heading: Agreed procedure
sections.body: Parties are free to agree on a procedure for appointing the arbitrator or arbitrators.

sections.heading: Court appointment
sections.body: Where the agreed procedure fails or is not followed, a party may apply to the Court under section 11 for appointment.

sections.heading: Independence and impartiality
sections.body: Appointment is constrained by section 12 and the Schedules; a person ineligible to act cannot unilaterally appoint.

cases.name: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd.
cases.facts: Contract allowed one party's official to appoint the sole arbitrator; the other party challenged the unilateral appointment under section 11.
cases.issue: Can a person who is ineligible to act as arbitrator unilaterally appoint the sole arbitrator?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A person who is himself ineligible to act as arbitrator cannot nominate the sole arbitrator. Unilateral appointment by an interested party is impermissible.
cases.holding: Appointment set aside; Court appointed an independent sole arbitrator under section 11.
cases.relevance: Leading authority on independence and unilateral appointment under section 11 read with section 12 and the Schedules.

cases.name: TRF Ltd. v. Energo Engineering Projects Ltd.
cases.facts: Managing Director was named as arbitrator and also empowered to nominate a substitute; challenge under the 2015 amendments.
cases.issue: Whether an ineligible named arbitrator can nominate a substitute arbitrator.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Once a person becomes ineligible to act as arbitrator by operation of law, he also loses the power to nominate.
cases.holding: Nomination by the ineligible Managing Director was invalid.
cases.relevance: Predecessor to Perkins; establishes that ineligibility disables both acting and nominating.

cases.name: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
cases.facts: Reference concerning arbitrability and the standard of review under sections 8 and 11.
cases.issue: Scope of examination under section 11 at the appointment stage.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 11 review is aligned with section 8: prima facie examination of existence/validity; when in doubt, appoint and refer.
cases.holding: Limited judicial intervention at the appointment stage.
cases.relevance: Confirms the narrow gateway under section 11.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can an interested party unilaterally appoint a sole arbitrator under section 11?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Following TRF and Perkins Eastman, a person who is ineligible to act as arbitrator cannot unilaterally appoint the sole arbitrator.
